body: Dr. Avery Chen already sends tissue to Tempus. Last visit they asked about adding liquid at progression rather than waiting on a new biopsy.
Circulated the liquid-at-progression workflow with their nurse navigator. They still want liquid when tissue is insufficient rather than repeating a biopsy.
Asked for a one-pager the thoracic APP can keep covering when to add liquid at progression. No new assay pitch requested.
Dr. Jordan Chen is still on FMI for most solid-tumor orders. They want a clearer story for HER2-low therapy decisions before considering a switch.
Wanted a breast tumor-board example of HER2-low therapy selection before they will move any FMI volume.
Scheduled a drop-by after their next breast conference. Still comparing FMI versus a clearer HER2-low story.
Dr. Riley Chen asked whether HRD status is confirmed before later-line therapy. They are also tracking gyn academic trial eligibility.
Shared how other gyn oncologists confirm HRD before later-line therapy. They remain focused on academic trial windows.
Asked to review HRD reporting with their fellow before the next trial screening meeting. No change to the later-line confirmation concern.
Dr. Quinn Chen is concerned about turnaround time versus Guardant liquid. They remain interested in a thoracic liquid option if we can address that concern.
Still comparing Guardant liquid on turnaround. Open to a thoracic liquid conversation if we can speak to that concern without a new tissue workflow.
Asked to bring a one-slide turnaround comparison to their next thoracic meeting. Interest in a liquid option is unchanged.
Dr. Morgan Chen prefers the in-house lab for surgical gyn specimens. They are open to a send-out conversation if specimen flow stays simple.
Walked through a send-out kit that keeps surgical gyn specimen flow in their OR. They still prefer in-house unless that stays simple.
OR manager wants a dry-run of the send-out kit. Morgan remains open only if in-house handling does not get more complicated.
Dr. Casey Chen is unsure which lab they use for heme. They asked which tumor-only panel path to order so heme cases do not follow the solid-tumor plus-normal workflow.
Clarified the tumor-only heme path versus the solid-tumor plus-normal match. They still do not want heme orders to follow the solid-tumor workflow.
Asked for a one-line order tip their APPs can use for heme. Incumbent lab is still unclear.
Dr. Harper Chen already orders a lot of Tempus. Last visit they wanted better operational follow-through on pending cases rather than a new assay pitch.
Reviewed two pending cases that stalled in accessioning. They still want ops follow-through, not a new assay conversation.
Asked for a weekly pending-case ping to their MA. Retain the account; do not pitch a new assay.
Dr. Drew Chen still uses FMI at the independent practice. They asked how community gyn clinics get HRD findings without a long send-out.
Shared how other independent gyn clinics get HRD findings without a long send-out. They are still on FMI until that access story is clear.
Office manager asked for a community HRD one-pager before the next clinic huddle. Drew remains on FMI for now.
